capabilities.name: Sign-in, recovery and app shell
capabilities.rationale: Customers sign in, recover access and reach the app shell on Android and web; operators use a separate administrative identity domain with hardware-factor sessions and their own recovery, so the admin entry diverges by design (ADR-020 section 7).

capabilities.name: Consent, eligibility and device permissions
capabilities.rationale: Purpose consent and age eligibility apply on both customer platforms; SMS and notification-access permissions exist only on Android, whose capture depends on them (product/01 section 3.8). Consent is the customer's own decision, so the operator console has no consent destination.

capabilities.name: Debt status, strategies and scenarios
capabilities.rationale: Debt tracking and strategy decisions are the customer's own job on Android and web, where desktop web adds dense comparison and side-by-side derivation (product/08 section 8.2); the admin console is powerful over the system, not over user financial data (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Transactions, accounts, import and export
capabilities.rationale: Account, category and manual transaction management are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); operators cannot read transaction descriptions or balances by default (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Capture health, clarification and rules
capabilities.rationale: Automatic capture depends on Android-only permissions and stays on Android (product/01 section 3.8), so web resolves clarifications and manages rules without a capture-health view; operators never read raw message content (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Email and receipt capture
capabilities.rationale: Android is capture-first and web analysis-heavy (PenniLogic/docs#74 context); the pinned registry has no web or admin flow for mailbox or receipt capture, and raw message content never reaches operators (product/01 section 2.2). Whether web needs receipt upload is open for the IA review.

capabilities.name: Income, budgets, goals and net worth
capabilities.rationale: Web covers income and budgeting, goals and net worth for parity with Android (product/01 section 3.8); this is the customer's own planning data, which operators cannot browse (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Multi-currency reporting
capabilities.rationale: Per-currency overviews and reporting-currency changes serve the power user who compares accounts and currencies on a large screen (product/08 section 7, P05); the pinned registry has no Android or admin flow for them, which the IA review should confirm.

capabilities.name: Adaptive failures and debt widget
capabilities.rationale: The home-screen widget and constrained-device recovery are Android platform jobs; narrow web remains a complete management fallback instead of a widget (product/08 section 8.2), and operators have no customer surface.

capabilities.name: Split groups and settlement
capabilities.rationale: Splitting is explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); group expenses are user financial data that operators cannot browse (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Family, household and safe exit
capabilities.rationale: Family features are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); household data is shared only between users, so no operator destination exists that could reveal it (product/01 section 2.2).

capabilities.name: Assistant and provider settings
capabilities.rationale: AI and bring-your-own-key settings are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); operators configure providers, models, routing and spend caps for the whole system (product/01 section 2.2, CAP-016) and have no destination for a user's assistant history.

capabilities.name: Billing, notifications and retention
capabilities.rationale: Web covers billing, invoices and the cross-channel notification preference centre (product/01 section 3.8); retention milestones and digests have no web screen in the pinned registry. Operators change plans and refunds through their own capabilities, not the customer's billing pages.

capabilities.name: Trust, rights and support
capabilities.rationale: Customers raise rights and support requests on Android and web; operators fulfil them from redacted queues with independent approval and immutable audit, never by browsing records (product/08 sections 8.3 and 9.3).

capabilities.name: Operator access, lifecycle and production access
capabilities.rationale: Unmasking, elevation, operator lifecycle and production access are purpose-built operator flows in the separate admin console and identity domain (product/08 section 8.3, ADR-020 sections 3 and 7); customers have no operator destination.

capabilities.name: Plans, AI operations, audit and release evidence
capabilities.rationale: Plans, feature flags, quotas, AI providers and spend caps, aggregate analytics and audit review are the system powers of the admin console (product/01 section 2.2), and incidents and break-glass are operator destinations (product/08 section 8.3); customers see only their own plan and assistant settings.
